description: We are looking for a low-cost, high-impact solution.
summary:
The problem

On long space missions, astronauts live in conditions unlike anything on Earth, and medical support is far away. NASA’s medical research, meanwhile, is dense, specialised text with few ready-to-use numbers.

The solution

ASTROX  is an integrated system that goes beyond displaying readings: it tracks each astronaut’s current health and predicts what comes next. A dedicated machine-learning model for every vital sign achieves a low mean absolute error (MAE), and a Qwen 8B language model, connected to NASA research through RAG, answers health questions grounded in the source itself.

How it meets the challenge

It turns scattered research into direct answers and early warnings the crew can act on.

Why it matters and what sets it apart

It draws on official NASA research (NASA.gov) gathered in real spaceflight conditions, combines prediction and explanation in one system, and runs on a lightweight model that needs no powerful hardware, which makes it practical to deploy.
details:
Summary of the note and the repo (Safety_First: ASTRA × AstroX)

What the project is: a health self-check system for astronauts. A Flutter app (AstroX) records daily check-ins and works offline. A Python backend (ASTRA) analyses them and powers a chat assistant.

What the note says (your five judging answers):

  1. Who benefits: astronauts on space missions.
  2. Creativity: not just a monitor, but a full system that tracks current health and predicts future health, with one ML model per vital sign and a “very good” MAE.
  3. Solving a real challenge: NASA research is hard-to-read text with few numbers, so you connected a Qwen 8B LLM to it with RAG so it answers from the research.
  4. Scientific credibility: the sources are official NASA research (NASA.gov).
  5. Feasibility: Qwen is light enough to run without heavy hardware and is still accurate.

What the code does:

  • Anomaly detection: an IsolationForest model flags unusual patterns across a reading’s vitals.
  • Forecasting: one XGBoost model per vital predicts the next day’s values, but only after 4 consecutive days with 2 readings each.
  • Assistant: Qwen3-8B with RAG (Chroma + MiniLM embeddings). Every health statement must cite a retrieved NASA passage or the answer is rejected.
  • Running it: FastAPI on Google Colab through ngrok, protected by an API key, with tests on both the backend and the app
